t: Minimum Division Operations to Make Array Non-Decreasing — Prime-Chain DP
o: One operation replaces x by x divided by its greatest proper divisor, which equals x's smallest prime factor: 25 -> 5, 6 -> 3, and primes are stuck (dividing by 1 changes nothing). So each value can only descend along the chain x, spf(x), spf(spf(x)), ..., ending at a prime (or 1). We must make the array non-decreasing with the fewest total operations, or -1. Example [25,7]: lower 25 to 5 in one op, giving [5,7]. Example [7,7,6] is impossible because 7 cannot shrink below 7 while 6 can only become 3 or stay 6.
k: Dividing by the greatest proper divisor sends x to its smallest prime factor, so each element's reachable values form one strictly decreasing chain.
Greedy per-element minimization fails (reducing an earlier element more can be cheaper overall); a DP over chain positions with monotone pointers is needed.

a.i: For each element compute its descent chain by trial division. dp[t] = min total cost if element i takes chain value chain[t]. Transition: dp_cur[t] = (min dp_prev[t'] over prev values <= cur value) + t. Since both chains decrease, the qualifying t' form a suffix, maintained with a suffix-minimum and a moving pointer.
s: chain(x): repeatedly replace x by its smallest prime factor (trial division) until x is prime; collect values.
dp over chain of nums[0] is [0,1,2,...].
For each next element, build suffix minima of the previous dp; sweep t from the last chain value upward, advancing a pointer past prev values greater than cur[t].
If no state survives for some element, return -1; otherwise answer = min(dp).
a.t: O(n * sqrt(V) + n*L^2) — trial division builds chains (L <= ~20 since 2^20 > 1e6); the DP sweep is O(L) per element with amortized pointers.

a.n: Approach 2: Sieve of Smallest Prime Factors
a.i: Identical DP, but precompute spf for every value up to max(nums) with a sieve, making each chain construction O(log V) instead of O(sqrt(V)). Worth it when n is large relative to sqrt(V).
s: Sieve spf[0..max(nums)]: for each i, if spf[i]==i mark multiples.
Build each chain by repeated x = spf[x] until x is prime.
Run the same suffix-minimum pointer DP.
a.t: O(V log log V + n*L) — sieve preprocessing plus linear chain walks and DP sweeps.

w: Present the DP, emphasizing why naive greedy fails (example [25,7] forces paying 1 op on the earlier element). Pitfalls: primes are immutable (7 -> 7, not 7 -> 1), and the DP must compare chain values, not indices. Edge cases: all 1s costs 0; any element equal to 1 imposes no constraint. Follow-up: what if the operation were 'divide by any proper divisor'? Then every composite could reach any smaller divisor and the DP would run over full divisor lists.
